Requirements for the cooperative phase
This section shows the plain rules
Companion Animal Travel Desk Procedures

This section governs the handling of companion animals, their documents, and the service actions required before travel. All staff must act at once when a concern appears, and every step must support safety, comfort, and orderly boarding.

The welfare coordinator must review comfort needs before acceptance and must confirm that the animal can travel without preventable distress. The welcome team must prepare the passenger with clear guidance, calm wording, and direct next steps. Staff must check carrier condition, labeling, and fit, and must refuse any arrangement that does not protect the animal or the cabin environment. If a traveler presents incomplete papers, the desk must pause processing until the record is corrected.

At the station briefing, the senior agent must remind the team to speak plainly and keep all directions brief. The service record must note any feeding limits, mobility needs, or handling cautions. When a pet needs separation from the main flow, staff must guide the passenger without delay to the proper area and keep the tone respectful. The desk must never guess at animal condition, and it must never promise acceptance before review is complete.

Agent: <<FACT F027>> The escort line must remain open for urgent animal transfers, and the crew must follow the quarantine instruction without interruption. No employee may alter that instruction or place the animal in a different holding point unless the welfare coordinator approves the change.

Agent: <<FACT F002>> The lounge area must stay orderly, quiet, and ready for use by approved travelers and pets. The desk must track access carefully, keep supplies in place, and report any service failure at once.

If a traveler such as Sana Bianchi or Marcus Davis needs help understanding the process, staff must give concise support and confirm the next action before the passenger leaves the counter. When Fluffy or any other pet shows stress, the team must slow the pace, reduce noise, and alert the welfare coordinator without delay.

Report all exceptions to the duty supervisor and the welfare coordinator immediately.
